title: an arbitrary dynamic `import()` expression is unavailable in native code: it contributes the `TypeScript` requirement, so a native pin over a function reaching it fails to compile
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native and Wasm Targets': 'Arbitrary dynamic import expressions MUST initially be unavailable in native code. A future finite, statically enumerable import-set implementation MAY make some forms portable.' docs/DECISIONS.md 'TypeScript and native classification' (Locked) records the same rule. This obligation was previously recorded as unwritable because 'there is no native backend to reject it'. That reason no longer holds: the rule does not need a native backend, it needs the checked assertion that a function is native-eligible, and the native pin now supplies exactly that. `loadModule` is deliberately an ordinary synchronous function returning the Promise rather than an `async` function, because a pin over an `async` function is separately rejected by the JS reference — see a-pin-over-an-async-function-is-accepted, which is an xfail. Keeping the two apart means this case measures the dynamic-import classification and nothing else.
